conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment certification serves as a necessary safety barrier against systemic bias or functions as an administrative tollbooth that delays essential care.

positions.stance: Argues that static pre-market certification imposes lethal delays on patient care and protects institutional incumbents, and that rapid deployment with post-market telemetry is superior.
Maintains that mandatory pre-deployment verification is necessary to prevent structural errors from entering clinical and judicial workflows before post-hoc audits can catch them.

conflicts.point: Whether open telemetry and decentralized model weights can effectively replace pre-market certification or whether they merely multiply uncorrectable institutional bias across endpoints.

positions.stance: Maintains that open-weight procurement mandates and continuous runtime auditing allow independent auditors to detect and correct demographic drift within 90 days.
Argues that fine-tuning unaligned models strips out telemetry hooks and that decentralized distribution permanently locks systemic discrimination into local operations without central oversight.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment certification serves as a necessary safety barrier against systemic bias or functions as an administrative tollbooth that delays essential care.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position accounts for downstream harms and irreversible structural errors in clinical and judicial workflows. Static pre-market boards provide a vital gatekeeping function that prevents systemic bias from embedding into live patient and inmate data.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that pre-market delays cause measurable mortality rates that exceed the harms inflicted by unvalidated algorithmic errors.

verdicts.conflict: Whether open telemetry and decentralized model weights can effectively replace pre-market certification or whether they merely multiply uncorrectable institutional bias across endpoints.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist undercutter successfully demonstrates that telemetry measuring internal consistency against a biased baseline only stabilizes infected training distributions. Furthermore, proprietary trade secret protections identified by skeptics prevent compliance officers from auditing live model updates effectively.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Federal legislation compelling software vendors to open all internal model weights and telemetry adjustments to independent auditors without trade secret exemptions.
